Boost or cut the overall level
Changes the level without touching the equalization. The limiter keeps the boosted signal from clipping.
Blends part of each channel into the other ear, as with speakers. The effect is subtle and clearest on recordings with instruments panned hard to one side. The options go from lightest to strongest.
Settings below edit the active profile. Choosing a profile assigns it to the current output.

Raises the bass gradually from the low mids down, as a tone control does: half the boost at the frequency, all of it in the deep bass. The boost stays steady; the level comes down only as far as the track has no room for it (from its ReplayGain), so the rest of the music keeps its level.
Raises the bass below the frequency. The whole boost applies while the bass stays under the ceiling and shrinks as it gets louder, so heavy bass lines are not pushed into clipping.

Audio is processed this far ahead of what you hear. A longer buffer rides out the moments when the phone gives the app little time (screen off, busy phone) without dropouts, but changes to the sound (equalizer, crossfeed, profiles) are heard that much later. Automatic starts at 2 s and adds a second after each dropout, up to 5 s. A new length applies after the next skip, seek or stop.

While playing, the player waits until the buffer needs more audio instead of checking every 10 ms. Saves processor time and battery with the screen off and avoids dropouts with demanding effects, without needing a longer buffer. Applies the next time the player opens.
Keep the screen on while playing
Only while music plays; when paused the screen turns off as usual.

Music player for local files and lists, with its own sound processing: gapless, crossfade, ReplayGain, silence trimming, equalizer, crossfeed, compressor and limiter.
Attacca is free software under the MIT license.
Open source libraries used by the app. Tap one to open its project page and full license.
Crossfeed: Bauer stereophonic-to-binaural filter design. Equalizer and tone filters: RBJ Audio EQ Cookbook biquads. Loudness: ReplayGain tags. All sound processing is implemented in the app itself.
Tap to choose the folder where your M3U8 lists are saved

To also start when the player is closed, Attacca needs the nearby devices permission, to be allowed to open its screen (display over other apps) and to run in the background (no battery optimization).

Chaining compares how each track ends with how the others start. Only the first and last seconds of each file are decoded, once; changed files are analysed again. It runs at low priority, so you can keep using the app and listening meanwhile. Without background analysis, the tracks of a list are analysed when you chain it.

Chain list (in the menu of the current list) starts with the playing track and always follows with the remaining one whose start sounds most like the end of the previous — tempo, timbre, activity, key and notes — then moves tracks around so no transition is left far worse than the rest.
How much of the end of a track is compared with the start of the next. Changing it means analysing every track again.
With %1$d s, all tracks have to be analysed again (the music folder, or each list when you chain it). Change it?
Files analysed at the same time
More is faster but uses more battery and warms the phone; this phone has %1$d cores. Takes effect from the next analysis. Playback always keeps priority.
Keep the screen on while analysing

With the screen off the phone slows itself down to save battery, and analysing the music folder can take several times longer. With this on, the screen stays on while Attacca is open and the folder is being read or analysed; better with the phone plugged in and the brightness low.

Tap a topic to open it. The tips over each screen come back with every new version (Settings → Appearance).

• Allow access to your files when asked: Attacca plays music and lists straight from your folders. The first time, a welcome screen helps you choose the music folder or restore a backup.
• Choose your music folder in Settings → Library and let it scan: tags are read once and kept, so sorting and searching big lists is fast, and exported lists stay valid on other devices.
• Open a folder from Folders, a list from Lists, or a file or playlist from another app with “Open with”.
• The side menu (swipe right on Now playing, the navigator button there, or ☰ in the main sections) leads to every part of the app and to the lists you played last.

• Tap the box with the title, artist and album to see everything about the file: pictures, format, analysis and tags. Its ⋮ menu has lyrics, the tag editor, go to folder, create a list from the track and the inclusion list.
• The list box shows the list’s name, the position in it, track number, year and genre; tap it for the current list.
• The waveform is the seek bar. Dimmed parts are trimmed silence or the crossfade. Tap the time to switch between elapsed and remaining.
• Swipe across the cover or double tap near one of its edges for the actions you choose in Settings → Gestures on the cover.
• Swipe left on the screen to open the current list, right for the side menu.
• Bookmark button: a tap saves the position, a long press opens your bookmarks. Other buttons: sleep timer, favorite, sound, lyrics, speed, A-B repeat…
• What Now playing shows, and where, depends on the theme (see Themes).
• Long press the cover to open the settings of its gestures.

• My lists are the lists you saved; Generated holds the lists made by mood and family; Opened lists are playlists opened from other folders or apps.
• The save button stores the playing list as one of yours, at the same track and position.
• Long press a list to select it; select a whole group with its checkbox. With lists selected you can delete them, and with one saved list selected, rename it: its settings, resume point and devices follow the new name.
• Drag the handle on the right to put the lists of a group in your own order.
• The lists folder opens a browser on the folder where other apps save M3U8 lists.
• In a saved list, the buttons under its title change it without playing it: chain, chain by albums, mix albums, group, sort, settings and tools. A list that is not yours is saved as a new one of yours. Settings → Chaining can keep every list made from a track, and the generated ones, as they start playing.

• Tap a folder to open it and a file to play its folder from there; Back goes up a folder.
• “Play folder” at the top plays the folder, with or without its subfolders.
• Long press to select files; then play them, add them to the current list or to any list.
• The ⋮ of each row offers create a list from the track and the inclusion list.
• The music browser and the lists browser each remember where you left them.

• Attacca processes the sound itself, in this order: ReplayGain and preamp, crossfade, 10-band equalizer, bass boost, stereo width and balance, crossfeed or virtual speakers, compressor and limiter.
• Each output (speaker, headphones, each Bluetooth device…) has its own sound profile, switched automatically.
• Crossfade and silence trimming are set in Settings and can be changed per list; albums can stay gapless.
• To keep the phone or other apps from adding their own equalizer on top, see Settings → Car and background → Sound effects of the phone.

• Every output seen is listed with its profile, a fixed volume if you want one and a list to continue.\n• A device can follow the last list played on it and start playing when it connects, even with the player closed (it needs the nearby devices permission, opening the app from the background and no battery optimization; the buttons there ask for them).

• Chaining compares how each track ends with how the others start: tempo, timbre, activity, key and notes. Tracks are analysed once, in the background, when you chain a list or for the whole music folder (Settings → Chaining).
• From the analysis each track gets a mood (energetic, cheerful, calm, melancholic, tense) and a sound family: tracks that sound alike, found in your collection by a sound recognition network Attacca runs on the phone itself. The same tells which tracks are closest to a track.
• Lists → Generated makes one chained list per mood and family. “Create list from this track” makes a list of the closest tracks, chained from it.
• Filters: artist, genre, years, tempo, track length (1 to 20 minutes unless changed), energy, mood and voice; 150 tracks per list unless changed. “Fit the filters to the track” sets them around the track, as tight as they can be while leaving ten times the tracks asked for.
• Analysing the whole folder is much faster with the screen on: Settings → Chaining → “Keep the screen on while analysing”.

• An M3U8 list that works as an allow list or a block list for the generated lists and for “Keep only included”.
• Add or take out tracks, albums, artists and folders from their menus; the rules are kept in a text file next to the list, so new files in those folders, albums or artists join after each scan.
• An orange “!” marks a track left out (also next to the title in Now playing); “◐” marks a folder with part of its music left out.
• Settings → Inclusion list shows the rules and the resulting list.
• Attacca Desktop on the PC can use the same list or its rules file.

• With the screen off the phone saves energy, and the audio can stall with demanding effects. The audio buffer set to Automatic grows by a second after each dropout, up to 5 s; the dropouts detected are counted in Settings → Car and background.\n• “Fewer wake-ups” lets the player rest until the buffer needs more audio: less battery and fewer dropouts.\n• Long jobs (scanning, analysing) run at low priority and show their progress in a notification.

• Settings are grouped in pages: playback, crossfade, silence skipping, listening, appearance, gestures, library, chaining, inclusion list, car and background, language and backup.\n• Backup saves settings, profiles, caches and lists in one zip file, to restore them on this or another phone.\n• The language of the app can differ from the phone’s.
• The flag at the top of the side menu changes the language; every language is also named in English there, so you can always find your way back.

• The pass over the music folder also finds where the sound of each track starts and ends, from its first and last seconds. Settings → Chaining can also do that for the whole folder at once, or analyse the loudness and waveform of every track (slow: whole files are decoded).

• In the car, Android Auto browses the current list, your lists, the generated and recent ones, and the music folder. Album and favorite buttons can be added in Settings → Car and background.\n• The home-screen widget shows the cover, the title and the controls, and works with the app closed; add it from Settings → Appearance.

Attacca never offers its audio to equalizer apps, and with this on it also takes over the standard Android effects of its audio and keeps them off, so an app that finds it cannot change the sound. Effects applied to everything the phone plays (Dolby and similar, or apps that capture all audio) act after Attacca and can only be turned off in their own settings. Applies the next time the player opens.

Other sound effects on this phone

For the sound you set in Attacca, turn them off or exclude Attacca in them (Settings → Car and background has more).

Welcome! Let’s get your music ready.
Attacca reads its tags once, in the background, so big lists sort and search fast and your lists also work on other devices. You can change it later in Settings → Library.
Coming from another phone or a reinstall: settings, lists, the music folder and its scan come back as they were, with nothing to scan again.

To play your folders and lists.

Attacca [atˈtakka]: in music, go straight on to the next movement, without a pause.
Files without ReplayGain tags are measured (EBU R128) before they play and get their own track and album gain; this gain applies only until then.
Add the widget to the home screen

By folder, each disc of a double album or of a box set (CD1, CD2…) counts as an album of its own and plays apart; by tag, all the discs of an album play together as one. Also for Reorder by random albums.

The analysed tracks of the music folder with their moods, sound families and chaining edges in one file (.bpcr2), for the Rockbox plugin and the web list generator: they make chained lists from it without measuring anything.
Where the player sees this music folder, e.g. /<microSD1>/Music on a memory card or /<HDD0>/Music in its own storage.

Your themes are files in Music/Attacca/Themes (pictures and fonts in a folder of the same name), so they can also be changed by hand. ⋮ saves any theme as a zip to share it; Import a theme takes one back. Start one from any theme with the copy button.
There is no theme in that file.

The themes that come with Attacca. Use one and a copy of it joins your themes in Settings → Appearance: edit it or delete it as you like, the original stays here (and gets the improvements of new versions of the app).
Light and dark, as the phone

• Settings → Appearance lists your themes and the two System ones: tap one to use it. The copy button starts a new theme from any of them; ✎ edits one of yours; ⋮ saves it as a zip or deletes it.
• The theme gallery (in Appearance and here below) has the themes that come with the app: Use puts a copy of one among yours, which you can change or delete freely; the originals stay in the gallery.
• Import a theme takes a zip (or a theme JSON) shared by someone else. Your themes stay as plain files in Music/Attacca/Themes, so they can also be edited by hand.
• A theme can have a light and a dark version and follow the phone’s light or dark mode.
• The editor changes the colors (the picker also offers the cover’s colors and warns about text that would be hard to read), the corners, the text size, the fonts (also your own TTF or OTF files), the backgrounds and the app’s icons. Undo goes back step by step; nothing changes until you save it or use it.
• Its preview shows the colors or the whole Now playing, also in landscape.
Blurred album art behind every screen
The playing track’s cover, blurred and softened, behind the lists, folders, settings and the other screens, over the theme’s own pictures. Needs Android 12 or later to blur.
Blurring needs Android 12 or later: here the cover shows sharp.
With both versions, a picture chosen for a screen that already has one is for the version being edited: the other keeps its own (a sunny day by day, a starry sky by night).

• Search, select (long press), drag to reorder, and sort by title, artist, album, track, year, file, path, date or duration from the ⋮ menu.
• Group by album, artist, year or folder: groups can be collapsed and moved as a whole.
• Reorder by random albums keeps every album together and its tracks in order, and spreads the albums of each artist across the whole list. Albums go by their album tag or by folder (Settings → Playback): by folder, each disc of a double album or a box set plays apart.
• Chain list orders the tracks so each one leads into the next, starting with the playing one.
• Each row ends with the track’s length; the bottom line shows the position, the total time and the size of the list.
• Each list remembers its own shuffle, repeat, ReplayGain, silence trimming and crossfade.
• The buttons under the title save, chain (track by track or by albums), group, sort and set up the list; the ⋮ menu has the rest.

• Backup also exports and imports the library analysis (.attlib) for Attacca Desktop on the PC or another phone: tags, silences, loudness, chaining edges and features. What was measured there is not measured again.\n• Export the library for players writes the .bpcr2 file the Rockbox plugin and the web list generator use, with the music folder as the player sees it.

• Gapless playback, crossfade and silence trimming are set in Settings and can be changed per list; albums can stay gapless.
• Files without ReplayGain tags are measured (EBU R128) before they play and get their own track and album gain.
• After a long pause, playback first goes back a few seconds to pick up the thread (Settings → Playback).
• Album shuffle takes albums by their tag (all discs together) or by folder (each disc apart), as set in Settings → Playback.
• The sleep timer stops after some minutes, at the end of the track or at a set time, fading out; speed, A-B repeat and bookmarks are on the buttons of Now playing; lyrics come from the tags.

• Now playing layout: add, remove and move its parts (cover, title box, list box, progress bar, rows of up to 7 buttons among 28, information lines, boxes and space). A box holds other parts, one under the other or side by side with a width each, framed, with a picture or with the playing track’s cover (whole, cropped or stretched, softened and blurred). Each line of the title and list boxes has its own text size. Information lines take any field of the track, also its mood and sound family, e.g. {format}[ · {bitrate}]: what is in [ ] only shows when it has a value. Landscape follows the same layout or one of its own.\n• When a screen is short, or the text or display size is big, the parts are drawn smaller so they all show, and the cover keeps a fair size.\n• The title and list boxes can show the next track (title and artist), as can any information line with {next} and {nextartist}; the themes with a list box show it there.

• Your own pictures: backgrounds for Now playing and each screen, pictures for boxes and icons for any button. With both versions a background can have one picture by day and another by night. A tinted icon takes the theme’s colors; one shown as it is becomes the whole button (like a key), lit with the accent color while it is on.\n• Settings → Appearance can also put the playing track’s cover, blurred, behind every screen.\n• Each theme is a JSON file, with its pictures, in Music/Attacca/Themes, and goes in the backup.

A track counts as played once half of it, or four minutes, has been heard (seeking ahead does not count); as skipped when you move to another one before that. They make the lists By listening (Lists) and the Listened filter when generating lists.
Keep a listening log for scrobbling

Each track played is added to %1$s in the standard format of portable players: a scrobbling tool on a computer sends it on to your account. Attacca itself does not use the Internet. Tracks without an artist or shorter than 30 s are not logged.
Once the log has been sent, start a new one so the same tracks are not sent twice; the old one is kept with the date in its name.

How the tracks blend: crossfade, mix (the ending track plays out whole), custom, or automatic, which decides each transition by how the tracks end and start. Skips by hand can blend too, from the instant heard.\n• Gapless means the next track of the same album: tracks of one album that a generated or shuffled list puts together blend like any others.

For the phone speaker or small earbuds, which cannot play deep bass: adds the harmonics of the bass below the cutoff, from which the ear hears the missing bass. It does not raise the bass itself (dynamic bass does that); with good headphones it is not needed.

• The EQ lowers the level by its highest boost (precut), so raising a band does not push the music into the limiter. Virtual bass adds the harmonics of the deep bass for the phone speaker or small earbuds. Channels: mono, one channel on both sides, swapped or karaoke. The compressor can set its makeup gain itself.\n• Every setting moves smoothly while you change it: dragging a slider never clicks.

• Bass boost has two curves. Gentle (the usual one) raises the bass gradually from the low mids down, as the bass control of a stereo does, and keeps the boost steady: the level comes down only as far as the track has no room for it, so the rest of the music keeps its level. Deep lifts only the deep bass and backs off when the bass gets loud.

• The sleep timer can also wait for the end of the album, of the artist’s tracks or of the list; that last track plays out whole, without crossfade.\n• When a folder played from Folders ends, playback can go on with the next folder or a random one (Settings → Playback). When a list ends, Now playing is left empty; Play starts it again.\n• Go to the end (track menu, cover gestures, a button of the layout) jumps to the last seconds of the track.

They are not saved into the list. Not in shuffle or with repeat, nor for a folder that goes on with other folders. Needs the analysis for chaining. Each list can say otherwise (list settings).

They are made again after each scan and each time they are opened, and stay ordinary M3U8 files with their rules in a .smart.txt next to them.\n• Endless lists (Settings → Playback, or each list’s settings): when a list is about to end, similar tracks chained from its last one are added, so the music goes on.
New smart list: a list made from conditions (genre, years, mood, what you have not heard lately…) that keeps itself up to date.

The landscape button opens Attacca O\'rama: the song as a moving landscape, at its pace.

• Attacca O\'rama (the landscape button, the track menu ⋮ or a cover gesture) shows the playing song as a moving landscape. The land is the song\'s waveform: loud parts are hills and tall buildings. The world comes from its mood and sound family: a dark land of castles, a city by day or a neon city at night, the seaside, meadows and mountains, a cold sea with icebergs adrift, space; with some of the cover\'s colours. The weather comes from how it sounds: storms with heavy, dark music, a high sun with bright music, clouds and rain with sad songs. Someone or something crosses it at the pace of the music and moves with it (a rider, a runner, a car, a cyclist, a walker, someone on an iceberg, a spaceship). Each track is a level that turns into the next. Below, a small player: tap or drag the map of this track and the next to move in them. Upright or wide; 30 fps saves battery.

• In O\'rama the traveller hops, flips, does cartwheels and wheelies with the beats, and others pass by now and then (birds, animals, flying saucers, fireworks…); louder parts bring more things along the way. The track\'s record with its cover turns up too: adrift at sea, flown as a kite, half buried on the moon, on a billboard or a banner. The small player shows where the track is and how long it lasts; tap «Next» to open the current list. The whole screen button leaves the landscape alone: tap it to bring the rest back. Long stretches far quieter or louder than the rest of a track (a ballad turning into hard rock) change its world for a while; tracks alike in a row get another traveller, hour or shades. Birds, trees, lights and animals move to the beat too. The heart adds the track to Favorites. The view comes closer in quiet parts and opens up in loud ones; at the track\'s peak something big happens (a rainbow, a shower of stars, fireworks). On the way: bridges, tunnels, villages, stations, big wheels, ruins, arches of ice, rockets taking off; now and then a dog, a bird or a drone keeps the traveller company. Before the end a sign shows the next track, and the level ends at a finish arch.

• Under the track\'s title O\'rama shows its mood and sound family. The sign before the end also says where the next track is in the list (7/23), and the level ends at a gate into the next track\'s world: a walled town\'s gate, a gate in a fence, a barrier that lifts, a neon arch, bunting by the sea, a gate of ice or a ring into space. The traveller takes the accent colour, light or dark enough to stand out from what is behind it, and has a light of its own in dark places: in a tunnel it takes the torch at the way in and leaves it at the way out (a car switches its lights on, a bike its lamp). Bikes, cars and horses lean with the slopes; legs and arms bend at the knees and elbows; houses, ruins and domes on the way hide the traveller as it goes behind them. The record\'s sleeve shows the album and the artist. On the right: close, whole screen and 30 / 60 fps, one under the other; when wide, the small player is a compact block in the corner.

• In O\'rama the buttons on the right (close, whole screen, frame rate) stay half tucked away so the sky shows: a tap brings them out, and they go back a few seconds later. The sun and the moon keep clear of the title and the buttons.
“Rediscover your music collection: hear it in new ways, with the best sound.”
• O\'rama also hides a few little surprises. Find them yourself!
